text.arabic_uthmani: فَلَمَّا ٱسْتَيْـَٔسُوا۟ مِنْهُ خَلَصُوا۟ نَجِيًّۭا ۖ قَالَ كَبِيرُهُمْ أَلَمْ تَعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ أَبَاكُمْ قَدْ أَخَذَ عَلَيْكُم مَّوْثِقًۭا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمِن قَبْلُ مَا فَرَّطتُمْ فِى يُوسُفَ ۖ فَلَنْ أَبْرَحَ ٱلْأَرْضَ حَتَّىٰ يَأْذَنَ لِىٓ أَبِىٓ أَوْ يَحْكُمَ ٱللَّهُ لِى ۖ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ ٱلْحَٰكِمِينَ

words.gloss_range: consecutive connector launching the when-clause as consequence of the prior legal refusal
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the opening temporal clause consequential: the failed legal appeal in 12:79 becomes the trigger for private crisis. The particle binds despair, withdrawal, and the elder’s speech into one cascading response rather than a neutral next event.

topics.headline: consequential temporal bridge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah opens as the consequence of 12:79 rather than as a fresh, detached scene.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows consistently treat the initial connector as discourse continuation and consequence after 12:79; QAC marks it as a coordinative or consecutive particle.

words.gloss_range: temporal adverb marking a completed event that releases the response clause
words.prose: {{ar:لَمَّا}} ({{tr:lammā}}) scopes over the completed despair and waits for the response at the withdrawal verb. The syntax makes the secret counsel an after-state of exhausted hope, not an independent strategy formed before the crisis lands.

topics.headline: completed crisis trigger
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the brothers’ despair as the completed threshold that releases their withdrawal.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a temporal adverb with past-tense conditional force, matching rows that locate the response at khalaṣū after the completed despair.

words.gloss_range: Form X perfect loss of hope concerning Benjamin after the blocked request
words.root_gloss_range: loss of hope and exhausted expectation; locally situational despair from failed negotiation, not theological hopelessness
words.prose: {{ar:ٱسْتَيْـَٔسُوا}} ({{tr:ʾistayʾasū}}) reports a completed arrival at despair, and {{ar:ي أ س}} ({{tr:y-ʾ-s}}) keeps that despair lexical pressure visible. The local object is practical and personal, Benjamin after the failed request, while Surah Yusuf later answers the same despair field with Jacob’s command not to despair of God’s relief (12:87) and the delayed-rescue pattern of 12:110. The hamza and rare Form X shape heighten the crisis without turning it into absolute theological hopelessness.

topics.headline: settled situational despair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the brothers reach a settled human dead end, which later Surah Yusuf hope-language will answer rather than endorse.
topics.reason: Form X, perfect aspect, the minhu complement, and the intra-surah echoes at 12:87 and 12:110 support the despair topic, while local context narrows it to a blocked rescue attempt.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus suffix completing the despair predicate with a concrete referent
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْهُ}} ({{tr:minhu}}) completes the despair predicate by carrying the prior referent forward. The tiny suffix keeps Benjamin inside the legal frame of 12:79, so the brothers despair of recovering him rather than of an undefined situation.

topics.headline: pronoun fixes the failed rescue target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the despair is not vague disappointment but despair concerning the detained brother already defined in 12:79.
topics.reason: The rows identify min after the despair verb and the 3ms suffix as resuming the brother from 12:79; QAC confirms the preposition plus pronoun structure.

words.gloss_range: intransitive withdrawal into a private separated state
words.root_gloss_range: separation, becoming clear or set apart, sincerity, and exclusive selection; locally the active branch is withdrawal into private counsel
words.prose: {{ar:خَلَصُوا}} ({{tr:khalaṣū}}) makes the brothers themselves the ones separated out; {{ar:خ ل ص}} ({{tr:kh-l-s}}) supplies the image of being set apart, but the local grammar keeps it to intransitive withdrawal. The word contrasts with more honorable Surah Yusuf separations such as Yusuf’s protected purity (12:24) and later exclusive appointment (12:54), so this privacy feels like anxious reckoning rather than purity by itself.

topics.headline: withdrawal into separated counsel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the brothers physically and socially separate from the public ruling before the elder’s rebuke emerges.
topics.reason: QAC marks a Form I perfect with intransitive local use; CRITICAL intertexts at 12:24 and 12:54 survive as contrast while the local sense remains withdrawal.

words.gloss_range: singular circumstantial state describing the group as confidential discussants
words.root_gloss_range: escape, rescue, survival, and confidential counsel; locally a ḥāl of private consultation with rescue overtones
words.prose: {{ar:نَجِيًّا}} ({{tr:najiyyan}}) supplies the manner of withdrawal: the group leaves as a confidential council. The singular state-word treats them as one enclosed deliberative unit, while {{ar:ن ج و}} ({{tr:n-j-w}}) lets the counsel carry a survival or escape pressure that fits the Benjamin crisis. Variant and wider najwā material sharpen the standard reading as secrecy, not social nobility or automatic blame.

topics.headline: singular state makes one confidential council
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the plural brothers become one enclosed crisis council, not merely several people moving away.
topics.reason: The bundle marks the word as an accusative ḥāl in singular form for a plural subject; variant rows are useful contrast but do not displace the standard confidential-counsel reading.

words.gloss_range: completed speech verb introducing the eldest’s direct discourse
words.root_gloss_range: saying, speaking, declaring, and reporting; locally the speech act launches the elder’s long rebuke and vow
words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) breaks the confidential group scene by letting one voice emerge, with no preamble or discourse particle softening the entry. The verb governs almost the entire remainder of the ayah, moving from remembered obligation to personal vow, and it follows Yusuf’s legal speech in 12:79 with the elder’s moral speech inside the surah’s wider network of accountable divine, paternal, and fraternal utterance.

topics.headline: one voice emerges from secrecy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the handoff from plural secret counsel to one authoritative internal speaker.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a perfect singular speech verb introducing direct speech; attachment evidence treats the following discourse as its quoted content.

words.gloss_range: possessed substantive adjective naming the group’s elder or greatest member as speaker
words.root_gloss_range: greatness, seniority, rank, magnitude, and weight; locally a role-title for the authoritative brother
words.prose: {{ar:كَبِيرُهُمْ}} ({{tr:kabīruhum}}) identifies the speaker as their elder or great one, and {{ar:ك ب ر}} ({{tr:k-b-r}}) lets age, rank, and moral weight remain in play without forcing one biographical label. The possessive suffix matters: the rebuke comes from within the brothers’ own body. The echo with the father called aged in 12:78 and the elder’s earlier moral separation in 12:10 makes the role more than a name substitute.

topics.headline: possessed elder title carries internal authority
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speaker is defined by seniority or authority inside the guilty group, not by an outside narrator’s name label.
topics.reason: The adjective functions substantively with a possessive suffix; CRITICAL rows support age, rank, and authority as a narrowed but live range.

words.gloss_range: interrogative plus jussive negation forming a rhetorical question that expects acknowledgment
words.prose: {{ar:أَلَمْ}} ({{tr:ʾalam}}) opens the rebuke as a negative rhetorical question. The form does not request information; it presses remembered knowledge into evidence and gives the moral argument a sharp interrogative edge.

topics.headline: negative question forces admitted knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the elder accuse by asking what they already know, not by giving new information.
topics.reason: QAC describes the a-lam construction as a rhetorical negative question expecting an affirmative answer, matching the accusation rows.

words.gloss_range: jussive second-person plural knowing with a factive covenant clause as object
words.root_gloss_range: knowing, recognizing, learning, and being aware; locally conceded knowledge of a specific covenantal fact
words.prose: {{ar:تَعْلَمُوا}} ({{tr:taʿlamū}}) makes the brothers’ own knowledge the ground of rebuke, and {{ar:ع ل م}} ({{tr:ʿ-l-m}}) keeps the accountability field active. The following factive clause is the content: their father had taken a pledge from them. In Surah Yusuf’s knowledge network, this human knowing is smaller than divine and paternal knowledge (12:77, 12:86, 12:96), but it is enough to incriminate them here.

topics.headline: knowledge becomes liability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the brothers are guilty as knowers, because the covenant content is already conceded to them.
topics.reason: The verb is governed by lam and takes the following anna-clause as object; intertext rows with 12:77, 12:86, and 12:96 are preserved as a narrowed knowledge contrast.

words.gloss_range: factive complementizer introducing the known covenant proposition
words.prose: {{ar:أَنَّ}} ({{tr:ʾanna}}) turns the next clause into the precise content of what the brothers know. It governs the father-term and packages the father’s action as an established evidentiary unit before the pledge is named.

topics.headline: factive clause packages the charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the father’s pledge-taking is presented as established content, not as a possibility open to denial.
topics.reason: Rows identify anna as factive after taʿlamū and as governing the accusative father-term; QAC confirms the subordinating accusative-particle function.

words.gloss_range: five-noun father term in accusative with plural possession under the factive clause
words.root_gloss_range: fatherhood, paternal relation, ancestry, and parental authority; locally Jacob as the brothers’ covenant-holding father
words.prose: {{ar:أَبَاكُمْ}} ({{tr:ʾabākum}}) is grammatically marked as the subject inside the factive clause and relationally marked as the brothers’ own father. The five-noun case form and suffix make Jacob both grammatically central and personally binding. The same father-root later shifts from your father to my father at word 33, moving from group accusation to individual accountability.

topics.headline: your father as bound authority
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the elder binds the addressees to their own father’s authority before shifting later to my father.
topics.reason: QAC marks the five-noun accusative form under anna; CRITICAL rows link this father term to the earlier pledge scene in 12:66 and the later first-person shift.

words.gloss_range: certainty particle before a perfect verb confirming an accomplished prior action
words.prose: {{ar:قَدْ}} ({{tr:qad}}) adds confirmation to the perfect verb that follows. The elder’s argument does not treat the covenant as hazy memory; it insists that the father has indeed already taken it.

topics.headline: confirmed completed pledge act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the pledge-taking as an already completed fact that cannot be evaded in the present crisis.
topics.reason: QAC identifies qad as a certainty particle before a past-tense verb, and the CRITICAL rows treat it as factual pressure in the rhetorical argument.

words.gloss_range: perfect taking verb governing the burdened party and pledge object
words.root_gloss_range: taking, seizing, receiving, exacting, and holding; locally covenantal exaction rather than physical seizure
words.prose: {{ar:أَخَذَ}} ({{tr:ʾakhadha}}) carries the force of taking into covenantal exaction: the father took a pledge upon them, not an object from the scene. {{ar:أ خ ذ}} ({{tr:ʾ-kh-dh}}) therefore links this clause to the legal-taking field around Benjamin, especially the refused wrongful taking of 12:79 and the juridical taking language of 12:76, while the local object narrows the action to a solemn obligation.

topics.headline: taking becomes covenant exaction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the contrast between wrongful taking refused in 12:79 and rightful pledge-taking recalled in 12:80.
topics.reason: The construction akhadha plus ʿalā plus person plus pledge object supports covenant exaction; local syntax blocks reading it as physical seizure.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus plural suffix marking the liable party of the pledge
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْكُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalaykum}}) names the brothers as the party on whom the pledge lies. Its over-or-upon force turns covenant liability into weight, and the second-person plural keeps the accusation collective.

topics.headline: burden placed upon the addressees
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices obligation spatialized as a burden on the brothers themselves.
topics.reason: Rows consistently identify ʿalā with the burdened party in the pledge-taking idiom; QAC confirms the preposition plus plural suffix.

words.gloss_range: accusative pledge object taken by the father and oriented to God
words.root_gloss_range: firmness, trust, binding, restraint, and covenant security; locally a concrete pledge instrument in the Benjamin guarantee
words.prose: {{ar:مَوْثِقًا}} ({{tr:mawthiqan}}) names the thing exacted, and {{ar:و ث ق}} ({{tr:w-th-q}}) makes it feel firm, bound, and trust-bearing. The rare mawthiq form is tied to the Benjamin pledge episode, especially the identical phrase in 12:66, so the elder is not inventing a new obligation; he is citing the earlier guarantee back to them.

topics.headline: rare concrete pledge instrument
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pledge is not vague sincerity but a rare, concrete binding object recalled from 12:66.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as the object of taking; CRITICAL rows preserve the rare form, the concrete binding image, and the 12:66 recall while narrowing it to this family pledge.

words.gloss_range: preposition linking the pledge to God as source, witness, guarantor, or solemn authority
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) completes the pledge with divine orientation. Whether heard as source, witness, guarantor, or oath authority, it prevents the covenant from being merely private family pressure.

topics.headline: pledge oriented from God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the family pledge is lifted into God-facing accountability.
topics.reason: The rows support several close values for min in the pledge formula; QAC confirms it governs the following divine name, so the topic is narrowed to divine orientation rather than one exclusive gloss.

words.gloss_range: genitive divine name in the pledge phrase as source or guarantor
words.root_gloss_range: divine name and God-centered worship; locally God as guarantor of the family pledge before appearing as judge
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:llāhi}}) closes the remembered covenant phrase with God as its source or guarantor. The same divine name returns as subject of judgment later in the ayah, so the speech moves from obligation under God to resolution by God.

topics.headline: God first appears as covenant guarantor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that God brackets the speech: first as pledge guarantor here, later as active judge at word 36.
topics.reason: QAC marks the divine name as genitive after min; CRITICAL rows explicitly pair word 18 with word 36 as covenant-guarantor and judge.

words.gloss_range: conjunction adding the older Yusuf failure to the present covenant charge
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) turns the speech from the current pledge to an earlier moral wound. The connector is additive but escalatory, making the present impasse part of a sequence of failures rather than an isolated accident.

topics.headline: connector stacks a prior failure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the elder is not making one charge but stacking Benjamin’s crisis on an older Yusuf failure.
topics.reason: Rows read the waw as coordination or resumption with the same rhetorical result: accumulated moral debt; QAC marks a conjunction.

words.gloss_range: preposition forming a temporal phrase of prior blame
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) starts the temporal reach backward. The phrase makes the earlier Yusuf failure a starting point of blame that stands behind the current crisis.

topics.headline: preposition reaches back before the pledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the elder move the accusation backward in time before Benjamin to the Yusuf wound.
topics.reason: CRITICAL rows consistently identify min qablu as a compound temporal phrase; QAC labels the local function as prepositional-temporal despite the compact tag.

words.gloss_range: temporal adverb cut off from an expressed genitive complement
words.root_gloss_range: frontness, facing, nearness, acceptance, and before-ness; locally anterior time that brings prior guilt into view
words.prose: {{ar:قَبْلُ}} ({{tr:qablu}}) stands as a temporal adverb whose missing complement is supplied by the known Yusuf story. {{ar:ق ب ل}} ({{tr:q-b-l}}) gives before-ness a facing quality: the elder makes the older failure visible before the present decision. The echo with Jacob’s earlier min qablu memory in 12:64 and the brothers’ prior-theft charge in 12:77 keeps this as remembered precedent, not abstract chronology.

topics.headline: before makes the past face them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the past placed in front of the brothers as evidence they must face before the vow.
topics.reason: QAC notes the indeterminate adverbial form; rows support spatial-facing imagery but local grammar narrows it to anterior recollection.

words.gloss_range: relative or maṣdarī particle compacting the Yusuf failure into a charge
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) packages the following failure into a compact grammatical payload. Its relative or nominalizing force lets the speech mean both what they failed in and their failing, preserving accusation without retelling the old plot.

topics.headline: compact charge without retelling
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the elder can indict the whole Yusuf episode without narrating it again.
topics.reason: The rows allow relative and maṣdarī readings; QAC treats it as a relative pronoun, so the output keeps the ambiguity as a narrowed compacting function.

words.gloss_range: Form II second-person plural accusation of dereliction in the matter of Yusuf
words.root_gloss_range: going ahead, exceeding, letting slip, neglecting, and falling short; locally intensified dereliction in responsibility
words.prose: {{ar:فَرَّطْتُمْ}} ({{tr:farraṭtum}}) directly assigns the brothers’ past failure to them in second-person plural. {{ar:ف ر ط}} ({{tr:f-r-t}}) can carry both excess and deficiency: they went wrong by letting duty slip. The Form II intensity and regret parallels such as 39:56 and 6:31 make the accusation morally heavy, while the local phrase restricts it to their failure concerning Yusuf.

topics.headline: intensive failure concerning Yusuf
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the older Yusuf event named as active collective dereliction, not merely loss or misfortune.
topics.reason: QAC marks Form II perfect addressed to the brothers; the fī Yūsuf complement narrows the root’s broad range to moral dereliction in that named matter.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the domain or matter in which negligence occurred
words.prose: {{ar:فِي}} ({{tr:fī}}) marks the domain of dereliction rather than a literal location. It makes Yusuf the field in which responsibility was violated, preventing the charge from remaining generic.

topics.headline: Yusuf becomes the domain of failure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Yusuf is not a loose object of the verb but the whole field in which their responsibility failed.
topics.reason: Rows identify fī after farraṭtum as abstract domain marking; QAC confirms it governs the proper name.

words.gloss_range: foreign proper name governed by the preposition while retaining marked diptote behavior
words.prose: {{ar:يُوسُفَ}} ({{tr:yūsufa}}) closes the remembered-failure unit with the surah’s central personal name. The diptote proper-name behavior keeps the grammar marked, while the direct naming refuses euphemism: Benjamin’s crisis is interpreted through the unresolved Yusuf wound.

topics.headline: Yusuf’s name closes the old charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the elder names Yusuf directly, collapsing the family’s unresolved wound into one proper name.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a foreign proper noun governed after fī; CRITICAL rows preserve both the diptote grammar and the narrative force of naming Yusuf.

words.gloss_range: consecutive particle moving from accusation to personal resolve
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) converts the charges into action. After the pledge and the Yusuf failure, the elder’s next move is not explanation but self-binding resolve; joined to the following future negation, the connector helps launch an emphatic vow rather than a loose intention.

topics.headline: consequence opens the vow
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the vow is the consequence of remembered covenant and older guilt.
topics.reason: The rows identify fa before lan as inferential or consecutive force introducing the vow; QAC marks the particle as consecutive or causative.

words.gloss_range: future negation particle governing the subjunctive refusal to leave
words.prose: {{ar:لَنْ}} ({{tr:lan}}) gives the refusal forward force and governs the verb that follows. The result is a solemn vow form: under the stated conditions, he will not leave.

topics.headline: strong future negation makes a vow
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the elder bind his future behavior, not merely describe his current mood.
topics.reason: QAC identifies lan as a subjunctive future negation particle; rows connect lan plus the following verb to formal vow structure.

words.gloss_range: first-person subjunctive refusal to depart or cease, with the land as object
words.root_gloss_range: departing, leaving, ceasing, and persisting under negation; locally non-departure from the land until release
words.prose: {{ar:أَبْرَحَ}} ({{tr:ʾabraḥa}}) is first-person singular under the negation, so the elder separates his own conduct from the group’s failure. {{ar:ب ر ح}} ({{tr:b-r-h}}) allows both not leaving and not ceasing, but the accusative land fixes the local sense as non-departure with a persistence undertone. Its rare vow pattern resonates with defined-endpoint persistence in 18:60 and contrasting attachment in 20:91.

topics.headline: I will not leave this land
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the elder’s repentance takes bodily form as staying put until authorized release.
topics.reason: QAC marks a first-person subjunctive verb governed by lan and connected to the land object; CRITICAL rows support broader cessation imagery only as secondary pressure.

words.gloss_range: definite land as the concrete object or place the elder refuses to leave
words.root_gloss_range: earth, land, territory, ground, and domain; locally the specific land or jurisdiction where Benjamin is held
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَرْضَ}} ({{tr:al-ʾarḍa}}) gives the vow a fixed place. {{ar:أ ر ض}} ({{tr:ʾ-r-d}}) can mean earth or territory, but the definite local phrase points to the land where Benjamin remains under authority. Surah Yusuf land language around Yusuf’s empowerment (12:21, 12:55, 12:56) makes the elder’s stay a vigil inside the very sphere he cannot control.

topics.headline: the land becomes the vigil site
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the vow is geographically fixed inside the authority space where the crisis must be resolved.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as accusative object of the departure verb; CRITICAL rows support Egypt or the local jurisdiction as the narrowed value.

words.gloss_range: particle governing the endpoint conditions for the refusal to leave
words.prose: {{ar:حَتَّى}} ({{tr:ḥattā}}) sets the endpoint of the refusal. It subordinates both later alternatives, paternal permission and divine judgment, so the vow can end only through authorized release.

topics.headline: until sets the release threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the vow is strict but not endless: it waits for a valid authority to release it.
topics.reason: QAC identifies ḥattā as governing the following subjunctive verb; rows show that the ʾaw branch remains inside the same endpoint structure.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive permission verb beginning the human-authority branch
words.root_gloss_range: ear, hearing, announcement, authorization, and permission; locally father-granted authorization to leave
words.prose: {{ar:يَأْذَنَ}} ({{tr:yaʾdhana}}) begins the first legitimate release branch. {{ar:أ ذ ن}} ({{tr:ʾ-dh-n}}) lets permission retain the sense of heard and acknowledged authorization, not mere ability. The placement of the to-me phrase before my father foregrounds the elder’s need for personal authorization before naming the paternal subject, and the same root’s announcement register in 12:70 sharpens the contrast: he waits for authorized speech rather than escaping the scene.

topics.headline: release by heard authorization
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the elder refuses self-release; he waits for permission specifically granted to him by his father.
topics.reason: QAC marks a subjunctive Form I verb governed by ḥattā with father as subject; rows support hearing-to-permission semantics while local syntax narrows it to paternal authorization.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus first-person suffix marking the elder as recipient of permission
words.prose: {{ar:لِي}} ({{tr:lī}}) places the elder himself between the permission verb and the father who can release him. Its first-person suffix makes the vow personal, and its repetition at word 37 frames both release branches around the speaker’s accountability.

topics.headline: permission directed to me
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the permission must cover the elder personally, not the brothers as an anonymous group.
topics.reason: Rows identify lī as beneficiary or recipient and note the repeated first-person pronoun envelope; QAC confirms the preposition plus suffix.

words.gloss_range: first-person possessed father-term as subject of the permission clause
words.root_gloss_range: fatherhood, paternal authority, and family relation; locally Jacob as the elder’s personal releasing authority
words.prose: {{ar:أَبِي}} ({{tr:ʾabī}}) makes the father the human authority who can release the vow, but the possessive has shifted. Earlier the elder said your father to press collective liability; here he says my father, binding himself personally before Jacob. The sequence places human paternal permission before the divine judgment branch without making self-authorization available.

topics.headline: my father replaces your father
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from accusing your father’s claim on the group to submitting myself to my father’s permission.
topics.reason: QAC marks the genitive five-noun father form with first-person suffix; CRITICAL rows support the contrast with word 12 and the human-authority role.

words.gloss_range: disjunctive conjunction separating paternal permission from divine judgment
words.prose: {{ar:أَوْ}} ({{tr:ʾaw}}) divides the endpoint into two sufficient branches: father’s permission or God’s judgment. The particle does not weaken the vow; it clarifies that either valid authority can release it, but the elder cannot release himself.

topics.headline: two sufficient release conditions
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the disjunction strengthens the vow by naming its only valid endpoints.
topics.reason: QAC marks a disjunctive conjunction; rows consistently treat it as balancing two subjunctive release conditions inside the same ḥattā structure.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive judgment verb coordinated with the permission branch
words.root_gloss_range: judging, deciding, ruling, wise ordering, and firmness; locally God’s future ruling as release condition
words.prose: {{ar:يَحْكُمَ}} ({{tr:yaḥkuma}}) heads the divine release branch, parallel to the father’s permission branch but higher in authority. {{ar:ح ك م}} ({{tr:h-k-m}}) carries judging, deciding, wise ordering, and firm settlement; the imperfect subjunctive keeps the ruling future and awaited. The verb is immediately answered by the closing judge-epithet, and it resonates with Surah Yusuf’s divine ḥukm statements at 12:40 and 12:67.

topics.headline: divine judgment as second endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the elder’s final alternative is not luck or escape but authoritative divine resolution.
topics.reason: QAC marks the verb as subjunctive and coordinated under ḥattā; CRITICAL rows support the yaḥkuma plus closing epithet link and the 12:40 and 12:67 judgment echoes.

words.gloss_range: nominative divine name as subject of the judgment verb
words.root_gloss_range: divine name and God-centered authority; locally God as active judge above the paternal authority
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:llāhu}}) names the subject of the judgment branch. Earlier God stood in the pledge phrase as guarantor; here God acts as judge. That bracketing makes the elder’s vow God-facing at both ends: the obligation was under God, and the outcome belongs to God.

topics.headline: God becomes the acting judge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the divine name shift from covenant guarantor earlier in the ayah to the subject who can resolve the crisis.
topics.reason: QAC marks the divine name as nominative subject of the verb; rows pair word 36 with word 18 and identify the final clause as centered on God.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus first-person suffix marking the speaker as beneficiary or affected party of divine judgment
words.prose: {{ar:لِي}} ({{tr:lī}}) repeats the first-person endpoint from the permission branch, but now with judgment rendered for or concerning the speaker. The two lī phrases frame the vow: permission to me, judgment for me, with the elder waiting between father and God.

topics.headline: judgment concerns the speaker personally
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that both release branches are syntactically tied to the elder’s personal accountability.
topics.reason: Rows distinguish directional permission at word 32 from beneficiary or affected-party judgment here while preserving the repeated syntactic frame.

words.gloss_range: conjunction opening an independent nominal evaluation after the conditions
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the closing nominal coda. After the vow and its two release conditions, the speech turns to characterizing God as the ground of the awaited judgment.

topics.headline: connector opens the theological coda
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the speech shift from release conditions to theological evaluation.
topics.reason: Rows treat wa-huwa as opening a nominal evaluative coda; QAC marks the conjunction that begins this transition.

words.gloss_range: independent pronoun beginning the nominal sentence and anchoring the epithet to God
words.prose: {{ar:هُوَ}} ({{tr:huwa}}) restates the divine subject in a separate nominal sentence. The pronoun isolates God as the one being evaluated, so the final epithet is not a continuation of the verbal clause but a stable theological assertion.

topics.headline: independent pronoun isolates God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final superlative belongs unambiguously to God and not to any human judge.
topics.reason: QAC identifies an independent 3ms pronoun as subject of the nominal sentence; rows support emphatic isolation and formulaic wa-huwa closing force.

words.gloss_range: elative construct head ranking divine judgment above all judges
words.root_gloss_range: goodness, better-ness, selection, superiority, and benefit; locally superlative praise of divine judgment with ethical goodness still present
words.prose: {{ar:خَيْرُ}} ({{tr:khayru}}) is the predicate head of the final construct phrase. {{ar:خ ي ر}} ({{tr:kh-y-r}}) lets goodness and superiority remain together: God is not merely one judge among others but the best and good judge in the matter. The formula echoes Jacob’s trust in God as best guardian at 12:64 and belongs to wider divine-epithet closings such as 7:87, 10:109, and 11:45.

topics.headline: best and good in the construct coda
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the coda praises both the supremacy and goodness of the judgment the elder awaits.
topics.reason: QAC marks an elative adjective in construct with the following plural; rows support primary superlative force while preserving ethical khayr pressure and concrete formula references.

words.gloss_range: plural active participle completing the construct and closing the ayah
words.root_gloss_range: judging, ruling, deciding, wise ordering, and exercising authority; locally the class of judges over whom God is supreme
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْحَٰكِمِينَ}} ({{tr:al-ḥākimīn}}) completes the construct and closes the ayah with a plural class of judges. {{ar:ح ك م}} ({{tr:h-k-m}}) echoes the earlier judgment verb at word 35, moving from an awaited act to an enduring role. The participle can include judging and ruling authority together, and the formula recalls divine adjudication language such as 7:87.

topics.headline: judges complete the judgment motif
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the awaited act of judgment turn into God’s enduring identity as supreme judge.
topics.reason: QAC marks a plural active participle governed by khayru in construct; rows preserve the same-root echo with word 35, the broader judge-ruler range, and the 7:87 formula.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence at words 2, 4, and 5 moves from exhausted hope through separation into confidential collective speech.
baseline_models.mechanism: The failure of public hope precipitates an extraction: the brothers filter themselves out of the larger scene, and that spatial separation becomes a protected deliberative chamber rather than mere dispersal.

activation_trace.role: Hope is cut off, supplying the pressure that terminates public bargaining.
Purification after admixture casts the withdrawal as filtering a mixed scene into a concentrated unit.
Exclusive separation supplies the social boundary around the brothers' council.
Confidential exchange turns the separated unit into one shared deliberative voice.

changed_reading.before: The brothers simply withdraw to discuss what to do.
changed_reading.after: Despair filters the public scene into a bounded council whose separation is itself part of how a new course can be generated.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The covenant at words 13-17 is answered by the elder's refusal at words 25-32 to leave the land before an authorized release.
baseline_models.mechanism: A bond once taken over the brothers becomes bodily restraint. The elder converts inherited obligation into voluntary custody by fixing himself to the ground until one of two competent authorities releases or decides his case.

activation_trace.role: Taking into one's hold gives the father's covenant the force of a claim laid upon the brothers.
A fastening bond materializes obligation as a restraint that can be carried in the body.
The confirmed pledge supplies the legal-social force behind the elder's self-binding.
Departure under negation becomes continued presence, implementing the restraint spatially.
Clinging and weighting toward the ground makes continued presence a bodily form of surety.
Authorization names the paternal channel by which the self-imposed restraint may end.
Adjudication supplies the alternative divine channel of release.

changed_reading.before: The elder stays behind because he is ashamed to face his father.
changed_reading.after: The elder makes his own body collateral for the covenant, entering voluntary territorial custody until paternal authorization or divine adjudication.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction at words 19-21 places an earlier failure immediately before the elder's open-ended stationing at words 25-32.
baseline_models.mechanism: The prior offense is not only recalled backward. Branches of precedence, negligent loss, and the one who goes ahead to wait let the failure become a temporal debt: the elder now holds a forward post until the unresolved authority or outcome arrives.

activation_trace.role: Precedence places the Joseph failure ahead of the present crisis as an already active condition.
Neglect that lets something escape supplies the unpaid loss carried from the earlier event.
A precursor who advances and waits converts remembered failure into a compensating forward station.
Heaviness assigns the elder the accumulated burden of both losses.

changed_reading.before: The elder cites the old offense as a reason for present guilt.
changed_reading.after: The old neglect remains temporally outstanding, and the elder answers it by becoming the one sent ahead to wait at the unresolved threshold.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Knowledge at word 9 opens a speech that ends with paternal permission, divine judgment, and the preference among judges at words 28-37.
baseline_models.mechanism: The elder does not choose a single sovereign path. He suspends movement between a human forum that can hear and authorize and a divine forum that can restrain, repair, judge, and choose the better outcome.

activation_trace.role: Disclosure to the knower frames the speech as an appeal to acknowledged facts.
Hearing with acceptance gives paternal permission an interpersonal evidentiary side.
License supplies the first formally sufficient release condition.
Restraint directed toward repair keeps divine judgment from being only punitive sentencing.
Choice among possible goods keeps the divine outcome open rather than predetermined.

changed_reading.before: The elder waits indefinitely for either his father or God to tell him what to do.
changed_reading.after: He holds the case open between two release forums, with divine judgment retaining corrective and elective possibilities beyond a verdict of blame.

context_deltas.mechanism: The private council becomes an evidence-triage chamber. It sits between concealed inward speech, public attribution, a possession-based detention rule, and the risk of putting a person in the wrong legal place.

activation_trace.role: Exclusive withdrawal provides the bounded room in which claims can be sorted.
Confidential exchange protects deliberation from the public accusations surrounding it.
Concealment in the interior supplies information present in the scene but withheld from the brothers.
Manifestation supplies the disclosure axis explicitly negated in the preceding scene.
Description presents public speech as a constructed account rather than transparent access to fact.
Finding supplies the stated evidentiary threshold for whom the ruler may hold.
Misplacing something in the wrong position marks the legal danger of substituting an unsupported detainee.

structural_cues: 12:77 juxtaposes concealed inward speech, non-disclosure, accusation, and description.
12:79 restricts taking to the person linked to the found goods.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies concealment, non-disclosure, public description, finding, and the danger of misplacement; I infer that these drive evidence triage inside the private council. A live alternative is an ordinary crisis consultation with no forensic function.

changed_reading.before: The separated brothers privately plan after a failed appeal.
changed_reading.after: They enter a protected evidentiary chamber because the public scene contains hidden knowledge, attributed guilt, and a strict rule against unsupported substitution.

context_deltas.mechanism: A proposed external substitution is refused, so the elder creates a noncoercive substitute arrangement: instead of being taken in the detained brother's place, he places and holds himself in the land.

activation_trace.role: Capture supplies the coercive mode of substitution that the preceding ruler refuses.
Nondeparture lets the elder reproduce custody without another captor.
Ground-bound persistence gives voluntary substitution a concrete site.
One person separated from the group supplies the offered substitute.
Place and standing supply the exchange slot the brothers ask another person to occupy.
The evidentiary finding blocks transfer of formal detention to an unlinked person.
Wrong placement explains why imposed substitution would be unjust while self-placement remains available.

structural_cues: 12:78 explicitly asks that one brother be taken in the detained brother's place.
12:79 explicitly refuses that exchange, and 12:80 immediately follows with the elder's self-stationing.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an offered substitute, its evidentiary rejection, and the elder's immediate refusal to depart; I infer a conversion from coerced exchange to voluntary self-custody. A live alternative is that the stay expresses shame without substitutive force.

changed_reading.before: The elder's stay is an isolated personal refusal to return.
changed_reading.after: The rejected substitute offer reappears in lawful form: the elder cannot replace the detainee in custody, so he replaces him in immobility.

context_deltas.mechanism: The brothers divide evidentiary labor. Some return with a testimony explicitly limited to what they know and open to corroboration, while the elder remains attached to the source location as a living site-marker.

activation_trace.role: Continued presence keeps one brother at the event's territorial end.
Known disclosure anchors the elder's instructions in an epistemic rather than merely emotional register.
Return sends the reporting party back while sharpening the contrast with the elder's fixed position.
Presence joined to observation defines the testimony the returning brothers can honestly offer.
Hiddenness marks the evidentiary domain their report expressly excludes.
Guardianship supplies the custody category whose negation bounds their responsibility for the unseen.
Truth realized in action supports the appeal to external checks on the report.

structural_cues: 12:81 limits testimony to acquired knowledge and disclaims guardianship over the unseen.
12:82 invites questioning of both settlement and caravan as independent corroboration.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a returning report, bounded testimony, unseen limits, and external corroboration; I infer that the elder's remaining preserves the other end of a distributed evidentiary chain. A live alternative is that his location serves penance only, not verification.

changed_reading.before: The elder remains while the others carry bad news home.
changed_reading.after: His immobility complements their bounded testimony by preserving a person at the source site while the report travels to the father.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later context explicitly contests the focus's exhausted hope. Persistent remembrance risks bodily depletion, yet the answer is sensory search and renewed openness to relief; the elder's ground-bound refusal can therefore be read as an incomplete, immobilized form of persistence rather than a final verdict.

activation_trace.role: Severed hope supplies the local closure that later commands reopen.
Nondeparture preserves persistence but initially leaves it without outward search.
Continued recollection keeps the absent Joseph cognitively present after others treat hope as exhausted.
Dissolution at the edge of destruction marks the bodily cost of persistence without resolution.
The same cutting of hope is now explicitly prohibited, retroactively localizing the focus's despair.
Tracking information converts inward persistence into an outward search practice.
Relief and rest supply the still-open outcome toward which search can move.

structural_cues: The branchless non-cessation construction in 12:85 mirrors the focus's negated departure.
12:87 pairs a direct prohibition of despair with an imperative to seek sensory traces.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated remembrance, bodily depletion, a prohibition of despair, sensory tracking, and relief; I infer that these recode focus despair as a mistaken local inference and the elder's stay as persistence not yet converted into search. A live alternative is simple chronological correction with no reinterpretation of the elder.

changed_reading.before: The brothers have reached a psychologically final end and the elder can only wait.
changed_reading.after: Their despair is a reversible closure; the elder preserves persistence, while later context shows that persistence must reopen into sensing and movement.

context_deltas.mechanism: The pericope distributes unbearable knowledge through distinct containment modes: Joseph keeps speech inside, the brothers isolate it in confidential council, and the father contains grief before directing its disclosure to God. The focus council is a middle form between total concealment and addressed release.

activation_trace.role: Exclusive separation creates a limited audience rather than unrestricted disclosure.
Confidential speech supplies the intermediate mode in which pressure is shared but contained.
Interior concealment supplies the fully inward endpoint of the disclosure spectrum.
Turning away creates another bounded space for grief outside the group's immediate exchange.
Held anger or anguish locates pressure in the interior before it is given an addressee.
Expressed complaint supplies deliberate disclosure rather than uncontrolled leakage.
Bringing the inwardly hidden into expression completes the movement from containment to addressed release.

structural_cues: 12:77 withholds Joseph's inward response from the brothers.
12:84-86 move from turning away and containment to complaint directed specifically to God.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies concealment, private counsel, withdrawal, inner containment, and addressed complaint; I infer a graded disclosure system in which the focus occupies the middle stage. A live alternative is that these are unrelated emotional reactions by different actors.

changed_reading.before: The brothers' private talk is simply secret strategy.
changed_reading.after: Their council is one node in a family-wide routing of unbearable knowledge, sharing pressure without either public exposure or total inward suppression.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's separation and immobility become temporary role differentiation inside a gathering process. One group returns, one elder remains, and later arrivals reverse the fragmentation into an explicitly complete family assembly.

activation_trace.role: Exclusive separation supplies the initial disassembly of the brothers from the public scene and from one another's routes.
Escape by separation supplies a provisional survival tactic rather than the final social form.
The elder's fixed location differentiates his route from the returning brothers.
Coming supplies the hoped-for reversal of dispersed routes.
Joining what has been dispersed gives the separation a prospective endpoint.
The circle of belonging identifies the social body to be restored.
Completion without missing parts supplies the pericope's answer to the focus's fragmentation.

structural_cues: 12:83 voices hope that all the dispersed sons will be brought back together.
12:93 closes the window with an imperative to bring the whole family.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a hoped-for gathering and a later command for complete family arrival; I infer that the focus's separation and stationary elder are temporary allocations within that return process. A live alternative is that reunion occurs despite, rather than through, the fragmentation.

changed_reading.before: The focus records the family's further disintegration after another loss.
changed_reading.after: Its separations distribute temporary roles whose latent horizon is the complete reassembly named later in the window.

context_deltas.mechanism: The old failure is recast as deficit within a wider economy of scant tender, full measure, voluntary surplus, and recompense. The elder's self-stationing can then function as embodied surety offered against a relational account he cannot otherwise settle.

activation_trace.role: Neglect that lets something be lost supplies the original relational shortfall.
A confirmed pledge supplies the obligation against which adequacy can be measured.
Grounded self-restraint lets the elder offer his continued presence as material surety.
Scant value supplies the context's explicit condition of insufficiency.
Completion without deficiency supplies the requested reversal of shortfall.
Comparison between measures turns adequacy into an explicit evaluative operation.
A voluntary due beyond exchange supplies surplus capable of repairing insufficiency.
Return corresponding to an act closes the context's sequence as an economy of recompense.

structural_cues: 12:88 moves in order from inferior tender to full measure, charitable surplus, and divine recompense.
The focus places a failed prior obligation beside a newly assumed bodily cost.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies prior neglect, pledge, scant payment, full measure, charity, and recompense; I infer a cross-domain ledger in which the elder's stay operates as surety for relational deficit. A live alternative is that the famine transaction and the elder's obligation remain separate economies.

changed_reading.before: The elder stays to bear moral guilt for an old failure.
changed_reading.after: He embodies collateral against an unbalanced relational account, while later scarcity and full measure expose the same deficit-to-repletion structure materially.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's appeal to knowledge and judgment opens a process later completed as recognition of action under ignorance, preservation of good effort, removal of reproach, covering of fault, and mercy. Judgment therefore remains accountable without ending in punishment.

activation_trace.role: Disclosure to knowledge begins the focus's demand that the brothers recognize what binds them.
Negligent loss supplies the remembered action requiring acknowledgment.
Corrective restraint keeps judgment oriented toward stopping harm and repairing order.
Produced action makes the brothers' treatment of Joseph the object of a second knowledge question.
Absence of knowledge qualifies the earlier action without erasing responsibility for it.
The negated loss of good effort supplies preservation rather than reciprocal destruction.
Recompense for action gives the judgment sequence a constructive outcome.
Blame for wrongdoing is explicitly removed at the moment recognition could have become condemnation.
Covering fault while protecting its bearer supplies a non-erasing form of release.
Tender mercy names the terminal disposition of the corrective process.

structural_cues: The elder's knowledge question in 12:80 is echoed by Joseph's knowledge question about the brothers' action in 12:89.
12:90-92 moves from preserved reward through confession to no reproach, forgiveness, and mercy.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies mirrored questions, action under ignorance, preserved reward, removed blame, forgiveness, and mercy; I infer a staged restorative judgment answering the elder's open appeal. A live alternative is that these later acts resolve the story without specifying what judgment in 12:80 means.

changed_reading.before: The elder awaits a divine verdict that may punish failure or free him from waiting.
changed_reading.after: The awaited judgment can be the whole restorative sequence: make the action knowable, preserve good, end reproach, cover fault, and return the family through mercy.

context_deltas.mechanism: The divine decision may manifest as perceptual and relational restoration rather than a courtroom utterance. A cast object reaches the father's face, right orientation and sight return, and separated persons are gathered.

activation_trace.role: Accurate wisdom allows judgment to take the form of making the hidden pattern rightly known.
Return from a condition gives judgment a restorative directional possibility.
Casting supplies the concrete transfer through which restoration reaches the father.
The right aspect of a matter links the face to recovered orientation, not surface appearance alone.
Insight of the heart makes restored perception an epistemic answer to the focus's uncertainty.
Rejoining the dispersed supplies the social effect of the restorative decision.

structural_cues: 12:93 couples the father's restored sight with an order for complete family arrival.
No separate courtroom pronouncement is needed within the window for the elder's requested outcome to become visible.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies casting, restored orientation and perception, and gathering; I infer that these effects can instantiate the divine judgment awaited in the focus. A live alternative is that they are consequences after judgment rather than the judgment's own mode.

changed_reading.before: God's judgment is expected as a verbal ruling on the elder's predicament.
changed_reading.after: Judgment may arrive eventfully: hidden relations become visible, perception returns, and the dispersed family is put back into right relation.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the packet's non-dominant mapping of the speech root toward fewness, bearing, and tremor rather than replacing the ordinary speech reading. It remains anchored to word 6 and to the elder's burden at word 7. Downstream prose should present it only as a split-map echo, never as the lexical gloss of the surface verb.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The speech at word 6 has a packet-supplied secondary mapped inventory, immediately followed by the elder and his assumption of the main burden.

activation_trace.role: Fewness lets the utterance sound like the voice left after the group's options have been reduced.
Taking up and rising under a load gives that reduced voice the function of bearing the group's unresolved duty.
Tremor under fear or anger preserves instability inside the apparently decisive declaration.
The main share of an affair identifies the elder as the one who takes up what remains.

changed_reading.before: The eldest brother delivers a firm decision for the group.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, a reduced and trembling remnant of group speech rises in the elder and takes up the affair's heaviest remaining share.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the context's action root carries a packet-supplied non-dominant mapping into the same mapped father inventory used by the focus. It remains anchored through the focus's two father occurrences and the elder's leadership. Downstream prose should call this reparative-fathering activation a formal cross-map resonance, not a claim that the context verb means fathering.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The elder repeatedly invokes the father at words 11 and 30 while assuming responsibility normally associated with family preservation.

activation_trace.role: Generation, nurture, and causing repair define the paternal function that governs the elder's self-accounting.
Leadership and rank make the elder the plausible temporary bearer of that family function.
The context's secondary mapping routes the brothers' produced action through an image of causing, nurturing, or repairing.

changed_reading.before: The elder remains answerable to his father as an older son.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, he tries to answer destructive brotherly action by occupying a temporary reparative father-function: preserving, taking responsibility, and awaiting a lawful return.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it crosses a form-distant stripping image in the focus with a later garment placed over a face. It remains anchored to the confidential-separation word at 12:80 and to concrete garment, casting, and sight roots at 12:93. Downstream prose should render it as a material reversal pattern, not as an etymological definition of confidential counsel.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus's confidential-separation root includes an extraction or stripping branch, while the window ends with a garment cast onto a face and perception restored.

activation_trace.role: Stripping or extracting supplies an uncovering image inside the formation of the private council.
A worn covering supplies the material inverse of stripping.
Casting actively places the covering where the reversal can occur.
Recovered sight supplies the paradoxical result: adding a cover produces disclosure.

changed_reading.before: The brothers strip themselves away from the public scene to see their predicament clearly in private.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the window alternates extraction and covering: a stripped-out council precedes a covering whose placement restores sight, so concealment and disclosure reverse material roles.

strongest_changes: The rejected person-for-person substitution becomes the elder's voluntary substitution in immobility.
The private council changes from generic strategy into evidence triage amid concealment, attribution, and bounded detention.
Later prohibition of despair and sensory search reopen the focus's exhausted hope and expose the elder's stay as persistence not yet mobilized.
The old failure enters a deficit-to-fullness economy, making the elder's body read as surety rather than remorse alone.
Divine judgment expands from possible sentence into recognition, preserved good, ended reproach, mercy, restored perception, and reunion.
summary.what_was_special: The focus concentrated obligation into spatial and bodily forms: filtering, fastening, ground-bound waiting, and conditional release. Context repeatedly reactivated those forms in forensic, affective, economic, perceptual, and restorative mechanisms without collapsing them into one final reading; split mapped roots also exposed a reduced-voice reading and a contained reparative-fathering possibility.
remaining_uncertainties: The chain-of-custody reading depends on treating the elder's continued location as evidentiary preservation rather than penance alone.
The deficit-ledger model is structurally coherent but crosses moral obligation with the later famine transaction.
Reunion may occur through the temporary separations or simply overcome them afterward.
The reduced-voice, reparative-fathering, and covering-reveals readings should remain explicitly exploratory because their branch mechanisms are form-distant.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Loss of hope separates the group into private counsel.** ي ء س B001, خ ل ص B004 (exclusive separation), and ن ج و B005 (private counsel) create withdrawal from public negotiation into an inner deliberative circle.
2. **Past neglect gives the covenant present weight.** و ث ق B004, ق ب ل B002, and ف ر ط B005 (shortfall/neglect) make Yusuf’s earlier loss a precedent that forbids casual return. I infer that memory transforms the promise from speech into liability.
3. **Remaining becomes self-imposed custody pending authorization or judgment.** ب ر ح B001 (remaining when negated), ء ذ ن B004, and ح ك م B002 anchor his refusal to leave. He creates a stationary obligation where the brother’s custody failed.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:83-90 answered the elder’s immobility with Jacob’s hope for total gathering and Yusuf’s eventual disclosure.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Loss of hope changing the forum rather than ending agency.** `ي ء س:B001` is loss of hope; `خ ل ص:B004` is exclusive separation from others, and `س ر ر:B001` includes confidential private speech. Once public persuasion fails, the brothers withdraw as a private counsel; there the elder reactivates covenant, prior failure, and a personal commitment to remain until permission or judgment. The packet supplies despair followed by concentrated deliberation; I infer that blocked external leverage turns action inward toward accountable role-allocation. *Istayʾasū ... khalaṣū najiyyan* reads as a procedural phase change, not paralysis.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:87 explicitly prohibits despair and converts hope into renewed search, confirming that the private council here was an altered mode of agency but not yet the story's final response to apparent closure.

baseline.text: Yusuf'tan umutlarını kesince aralarında gizlice konuşmak üzere ayrıldılar. Büyükleri dedi ki: "Babanızın Allah adına sizden sağlam bir söz aldığını ve daha önce Yusuf konusunda kusur ettiğinizi bilmiyor musunuz? Babam bana izin verinceye ya da Allah hakkımda hüküm verinceye kadar bu ülkeden ayrılmayacağım. O, hükmedenlerin en iyisidir.

findings.text: Kamusal ikna umudu bitince grubun özel görüşmeye ayrılması, çaresizliği eylemsizlik yerine sorumlulukların yeniden dağıtıldığı başka bir karar alanına çevirir.
Büyük kardeşin ülkede kalması, önceki kusur ve yeni söz karşısında izin ya da hüküm gelene kadar kendine uyguladığı bir gözetimdir.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, genel bir olumsuz bakıştan çok belirli bir umut ve beklentinin sona ermesiyle sınırlıdır; ettirgen biçimler bu çekirdeğin katılımcı yapısını değiştirir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım çıplak dalın umudu kesme çekirdeğini esas alır; listelenen eylem ve ad biçimleri bu çekirdeğin durum, süreç ve ettirgen gerçekleşmeleridir.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin beklediği bir şeyin gerçekleşeceğine dair umudunu ve olumlu beklentisini bütünüyle yitirmesidir. Ettirgen kullanımda başka biri, kişinin söz konusu şeyden umudunu kesmesine yol açar.

facets.statement: Beklenen şeyin gerçekleşeceğine ilişkin umut kesilir, olumlu beklenti ortadan kalkar ve kişi artık ona ulaşmayı beklemez.
Ettirgen gerçekleşmede bir kişi, başka bir kişinin belirli bir şeyden umudunu kesmesine ve umutsuzluğa düşmesine yol açar.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çerçevesi umudun kesilmesini, umutsuzluğa düşmeyi ve olumlu beklentinin kalmamasını aynı anlam alanında birleştirir; ayrıca bu duruma girme ile birini bu duruma düşürme arasındaki geçişi gösterir.

concept_gloss.text: umudu kesme veya birine umudunu kestirme
concept_gloss.applicability: Dalın hem kişinin kendi umudunu yitirmesini hem de başka birinin bu sonucu doğurmasını kapsayan en kısa bütünlüklü karşılığıdır.

error_profile.preserves: Umudun ve olumlu beklentinin sona ermesini, ayrıca ettirgen katılımcı değişimini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kişinin beklediği bir şeyin artık gerçekleşmeyeceğini düşünüp ona ilişkin umudunu yitirdiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kişinin kendi umudunu ve olumlu beklentisini bütünüyle yitirmesini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Duygusal sonucun öne çıktığı ve bağlamın hangi umut ya da beklentinin sona erdiğini açıkça gösterdiği cümlelerde doğaldır.

error_profile.preserves: Umut kalmamasıyla ortaya çıkan umutsuzluk durumunu korur.
error_profile.loses: Belirli bir beklentinin bilinçli biçimde sona ermesi işlemini tek başına açıkça göstermez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin sözleri ya da davranışlarıyla başka bir kişinin belirli bir sonuçtan umut kesmesine yol açtığı ettirgen bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Başka bir katılımcının umudun kesilmesine neden olması ilişkisini korur.
Olumlu bir sonuç beklememe yönünü kısmen korur.
error_profile.adds: Belirli bir umudun kesilmesinden bağımsız, genel ve süreğen bir olumsuz bakışı da kapsar.
error_profile.collision: Genel kişilik eğilimi veya dünya görüşü anlamıyla karışabilir.

error_profile.preserves: Kişinin olumsuz bir durum karşısındaki sıkışmışlığını korur.
error_profile.loses: Bir beklentinin gerçekleşmeyeceğine karar verip umudu kesme çekirdeğini silikleştirir.
error_profile.adds: Çözüm yolu veya hareket olanağı bulunmaması anlamını ekler.
error_profile.collision: Umut kaybından çok araç ve çözüm yokluğu bildiren ayrı kavramla çakışır.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da belirli bir şeyden, iyilikten veya esenlikten umut kesip artık olumlu sonuç beklememeyi anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Çekirdek işlem ve kapsam bakımından anlamlı bir ayrım yoktur; verilen özel bağlamlar birbirinin yerine geçebilirliği bozmaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Beklenen iyi sonucun gerçekleşmeyeceği düşüncesiyle umudun ve olumlu beklentinin sona ermesi.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Sevindirici bir sonucun gerçekleşebileceğine dair umut ve olumlu beklentinin sürmesi.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da gelecekte arzulanan bir sonucun gerçekleşip gerçekleşmeyeceğine yönelik beklentiyi düzenler.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal olumlu sonucun mümkün olduğuna yönelen umudu kurarken bu dal aynı eksende o umudun ortadan kalkmasını bildirir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Sekiz adayın tümü değerlendirildi. Doğrudan eş anlamlı dal ile açık karşıtlık kuran umut dalı yayımlandı; öteki adaylar ya bu iki sınırı yineliyor ya da istek, bekleyiş, yolculukta kalma ve benzeri daha uzak alanlara kayıyor.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه قطع الرجاء والقنوط وانتفاء الطمع، ويئس وأيس واستيأس، وتعديته بآيسه وأيأسه
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه معنى علم، ولا الأعلام كاليأس وإلياس
branches.source_phrase_ar: اليأس قطع الرجاء (maqayis)؛ اليأس ضد الرجاء (jamhara)؛ اليأس القنوط (sihah)؛ اليأس انتفاء الطمع (mufradat)؛ آيسه فلان من كذا فاستيأس منه بمعنى أيس (sihah)؛ أيس يأيس وآيسته أي أيأسته وهو اليأس والإياس (tahdhib)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, belirli soru cümlelerindeki eylemi belirli bir ağıza bağlayarak 'bilmek' diye açıklayan görüşleri aktarır; ancak aynı toplu ifade, sözcüğün dilde doğrudan bu anlam için konmuş olduğu iddiasını açıkça reddeden bir görüş de içerir. Bu nedenle dal bağımsız ve genel bir bilme anlamı olarak değil, kaynaklar arasında tartışmalı kalan sınırlı bir yorum olarak kurulmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnızca belirli soru bağlamlarında bilme diye açıklanan tartışmalı kullanımı kapsar; genel bilme kavramına veya ana umudu kesme dalına dönüştürülemez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak ve genel bir anlam varsayılmaz; kanıt yalnızca belirli soru cümlelerindeki, bir ağıza bağlanan ve başka bir açıklamayla itiraz edilen yorumu destekler.

concept_map.definition: Belirli soru cümlelerinde eylemin 'bilmek' anlamıyla açıklandığı, belirli bir ağıza bağlanan tartışmalı kullanımdır. Karşı görüş, bunun sözcüğün bağımsız sözlük anlamı olmadığını belirtir.

facets.statement: Belirli soru cümlelerindeki eylem, bir ağıza özgü kullanım olduğu ileri sürülerek 'bilmek' anlamıyla açıklanır.
Karşı açıklama, sözcüğün dilde doğrudan 'bilmek' anlamı için konmuş olduğunu reddeder ve bu okumayı bağımsız anlam saymaz.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kanıtın bir bölümü, belirli soru cümlelerindeki kullanımı bir ağıza bağlayarak 'bilmek' diye açıklar. Buna karşılık başka bir açıklama, bunun sözcüğün dilde doğrudan bilme anlamına geldiğini göstermediğini savunur; bu yüzden kullanım kaynaklar arasında tartışmalı ve sınırlıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yalnızca kanıtta belirtilen soru bağlamlarını, belirli bir ağıza bağlanma kaydını ve bağımsız anlam itirazını birlikte göstermek için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Önerilen bilme yorumunu, kullanımın sınırlılığını ve bu yorumun bağımsız anlam sayılmasına yönelik itirazı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yalnızca bilme yorumunu benimseyen açıklamaya göre, kanıtta belirtilen soru cümlelerinin akıcı çevirisinde kullanılabilir.

error_profile.preserves: Belirli soru cümleleri için önerilen bilme karşılığını korur.
error_profile.loses: Kullanımın belirli bir ağıza bağlanmasını ve bağımsız sözlük anlamı sayılmasına yönelik açık itirazı göstermez.
error_profile.collision: Kayıtsız kullanıldığında genel ve tartışmasız bilme anlamıyla karışır.

error_profile.preserves: Bilgi alanına ilişkin genel yönelimi korur.
error_profile.loses: Önerilen yorumdaki mevcut bilgi durumunu ve yorumun tartışmalı sınırını göstermez.
error_profile.adds: Daha önce bilinmeyen bir bilginin sonradan edinilmesi sürecini ekler.
error_profile.collision: Bilgi edinme eylemiyle bilgi sahibi olma durumu birbirine karışır.

error_profile.preserves: Aynı kökün ana dalıyla olan biçimsel bağlantıyı korur.
error_profile.loses: Bu dalı ayıran sınırlı bilme yorumunu bütünüyle ortadan kaldırır.
error_profile.adds: Bir beklentinin sona ermesi ve umutsuzluğa düşme anlamını getirir.
error_profile.collision: Doğrudan birinci dalın umudu kesme çekirdeğiyle çakışır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Belirli soru cümlelerinde bilme diye açıklanan, bir ağıza bağlanan ve bağımsız anlam niteliği tartışılan kullanım.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir beklentinin gerçekleşmeyeceğini düşünerek umudu bütünüyle kesme ve olumlu beklentiyi yitirme.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: tartışmalı bilme yorumu ile umudu kesme
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal aynı kök altında bağlantılı görünür; tartışma, soru bağlamındaki biçimin bilme karşılığı mı yoksa ana anlamla ilişkili bir kullanım mı olduğundadır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Birinci dalın çekirdeği umudun sona ermesidir; bu dal ise yalnızca belirli bağlamlarda ileri sürülen bilme yorumunu ve bu yorumun bağımsız anlam sayılmasına yönelik itirazı kaydeder. Genel kullanımda birbirlerinin yerine geçmezler.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Dokuz adayın tümü değerlendirildi. Dalın kararsız sınırını doğrudan açıklayan ana umudu kesme dalı yayımlandı; sanı, uzmanlık, bilgisizlik, ağlamaya hazırlanma, anlatma, açığa çıkarma ve bilgilendirme alanlarındaki öteki adaylar yalnızca uzak alan ortaklığı taşıyor.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه استعمال يئس وتيأس بمعنى علم في قول ألم تيأس وأفلم ييأس، على لغة من نسبها إلى النخع
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه أصل قطع الرجاء والقنوط إلا على تفسير من يجعل العلم لازما لليأس
branches.source_phrase_ar: ألم تيأس أي ألم تعلم (maqayis)؛ يئس أيضا بمعنى علم في لغة النخع (sihah)؛ أفلم ييأس أفلم يعلم (tahdhib)؛ ييأس بمعنى يعلم لغة للنخع (tahdhib)؛ ولم يرد أن اليأس موضوع في كلامهم للعلم (mufradat)

root_profile.summary: Kök, ana anlam olarak umudu ve olumlu beklentiyi bütünüyle yitirmeyi düzenler. Ayrı dalda ise belirli soru bağlamlarında bilme diye açıklanan, belirli bir ağıza bağlanan ve bağımsız anlam niteliği reddedilen tartışmalı bir kullanım bulunur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Toplu dal iddiası, bir şeyde önceden bulunan karışımın, bulanıklığın ya da kirin giderilmesini ve şeyin duru duruma gelmesini birlikte bildirir. Bu çerçeve hem bir nesneyi arıtma eylemini hem de nesnenin arınmış sonucunu kapsar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, önceki bir karışanın giderilmesini gerektirir; kurtulma, ulaşma, dinsel yöneliş ve özel yiyecek adları bu çıplak anlamın parçası değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dalın yalın durum anlamı ile bir öznenin nesneyi arıtmasını bildiren geçişli kullanım ayrı tutulur; başka yapılara bağlı kurtulma veya adanma anlamları buraya taşınmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyde önceden bulunan karışımı, bulanıklığı ya da kiri gidererek onu duru ve katkısız duruma getirme; geçişsiz kullanımda ise bu sonuca varmadır.

facets.statement: Bir şeyde daha önce bulunan karışım, bulanıklık ya da kir giderilir.
Giderme işleminin sonucu, şeyin duru ve katkısız bir duruma gelmesidir.
Geçişli kullanımda bir özne nesneyi arıtır; geçişsiz kullanımda nesnenin kendisi arınmış duruma gelir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıt, arıtma işlemi ile onun duru sonucunu aynı anlam çekirdeğinde birleştirir. Önceden var olan karışanın, bulanıklığın ya da kirin giderilmesi bu dalı doğuştan katkısız olma durumundan ayırır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Önceden karışmış veya bulanmış bir şeyi arıtma sürecini ve bunun duru sonucunu birlikte anlatan genel karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Hem karışanı giderme işlemini hem de ulaşılan duru sonucu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir öznenin nesnedeki bulanıklığı, kiri ya da karışanı giderdiği geçişli bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Etken arıtma işlemini ve karışanın giderilmesini eksiksiz korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Nesnenin karışandan kurtulup duru duruma geldiğini bildiren geçişsiz bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Nesnenin önceki karışandan sonra ulaştığı duru sonucu korur.
Nesnenin katkısız bir duruma gelmesi sonucunu korur.
error_profile.loses: Bir öznenin karışanı giderdiği geçişli işlemi açıkça anlatmaz.

error_profile.preserves: İstenmeyen bir öğenin giderilmesi yönünü kısmen korur.
error_profile.loses: Karışımın ayrılmasıyla ulaşılan duruluk sonucunu belirsiz bırakır.
error_profile.adds: Yüzey kiri giderme gibi bu dala özgü olmayan genel temizlik işlemlerini çağrıştırır.
error_profile.collision: Genel temizlik anlamıyla kolayca karışır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Önceden bulunan karışanın ya da bulanıklığın giderilmesiyle oluşan değişimi özellikle gerektirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Duru su, iyi bölüm veya zaten katkısız olan şey gibi işlem gerektirmeyen durumları da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da bir şeyin karışıksız ve duru olmasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal, şeyde daha önce bulunan karışanın giderilmesiyle ulaşılan duruluğu öne çıkarır. Komşu dal ise bir arıtma geçmişi gerektirmeden duruluk, katkısızlık ve bir şeyin iyi bölümü gibi daha geniş kullanımlara açılır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Karışım, bulanıklık veya kirin ardından oluşan duru sonucu çekirdeğe alır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Kusur, ayıp veya suçtan arındırma ve temizleme alanlarına da uzanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dalda da istenmeyen bir öğeyi gidererek şeyi daha temiz hale getirme vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın sınırı karışanı giderip duru bir sonuç elde etmektir. Komşu dal fiziksel karışanın yanı sıra kusur ve suç gibi değerlendirmeye bağlı yükleri gidermeyi de kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Önceki karışandan arınmaya götüren süreç ve durum değişikliği bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Hiç karıştırılmamış içecek ve tek başına yoğun renk gibi baştan beri yalın durumları kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: sonradan arınma ile baştan karışıksız olma
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da başka bir öğeyle karışmama niteliği bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal, önceki karışanın giderildiği bir dönüşümü bildirir. Komşu dal ise böyle bir dönüşüm olmadan karışıksızlığı ve kimi yoğun renk kullanımlarını adlandırır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Her tür nesnede karışanı giderip duru bir sonuca ulaşan genel süreci anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Yağ işleminde kullanılan katkı, çıkan öz, dip tortusu ve hurma şurubu gibi geleneksel yiyecek adlarını kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Yiyecek hazırlamadaki bazı kullanımlar ayırma ve arıtma düşüncesiyle ilişkilidir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal genel bir arıtma ve durulma anlamıdır. Komşu dal aynı imgeyle bağlantılı olsa da belirli yiyecek süreçlerindeki araç, ürün ve kalıntı adlarından oluşan özel bir söz varlığı kümesidir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi. En yakın genel duruluk ve arıtma dalları ile yiyecek alanındaki yerel dal yayımlandı; kurtulma, ulaşma, dinsel kullanım ve ilgisiz temizlik adayları çekirdeği keskinleştirmediği için elendi.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه خلوص الشيء وصفاؤه بعد شوب أو كدر أو درن، وتنقيته وتهذيبه حتى يصير خالصا.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه النجاة من حبالة أو منشب، ولا الوصول إلى شخص، ولا الإخلاص الديني إلا من جهة الصورة العامة للتنقية.
branches.source_phrase_ar: أصل واحد مطرد وهو تنقية الشيء وتهذيبه (maqayis)؛ خلص الشيء خلوصا (ayn;tahdhib)؛ صفيته من كدر أو درن (jamhara)؛ صار خالصا (sihah)؛ الخالص هو ما زال عنه شوبه بعد أن كان فيه (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Toplu dal iddiası, bir kişi ya da şeyin takılıp kaldığı bağdan sıyrılarak güvenli duruma geçmesini ve bir başkasının onu bu bağdan çıkarmasını açıkça birleştirir. Kaçma örneği bu kurtulma çekirdeğinin özel bir görünümüdür.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Önceden bir bağa, tuzağa ya da engelleyici duruma takılmış olma önemlidir; sıradan hareket, genel arınma ve bir hedefe ulaşma bu dalı oluşturmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Kendi kendine kurtulma, bir başkasını kurtarma ve kaçıp uzaklaşma kullanımları ayrı katılımcı yapılarıyla korunur; bunlar yalın bir duruluk anlamına genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişi ya da şeyin takıldığı bağdan, tuzaktan veya engelleyici durumdan sıyrılıp güvenli duruma geçmesi; geçişli kullanımda bir başkasının onu bu durumdan çıkarmasıdır.

facets.statement: Kurtulan kişi ya da şey önceden bir bağa, tuzağa veya engelleyici duruma takılmıştır.
Bu bağlı durumdan sıyrılma, güvenli ve serbest bir sonuca geçiş sağlar.
Geçişli kullanımda bir kurtarıcı, takılmış kişi ya da şeyi bağdan uzaklaştırır.
Kaçıp uzaklaşma, bağlı durumdan sıyrılmanın özel bir gerçekleşmesi olarak verilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıt, tuzağa veya başka bir bağa takıldıktan sonra kurtulmayı, birini bu bağdan kurtarmayı ve kaçışı aynı çekirdek çevresinde toplar. Yalnızca serbestçe gitmek değil, engelleyici bir ilişkiden çıkmak belirleyicidir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Kişinin ya da şeyin önceden yakalandığı, tutulduğu veya takıldığı bir durumdan sıyrılmasını anlatan genel karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Önceki bağlı durumu, ondan sıyrılmayı ve güvenli sonucu birlikte korur.
